title: Mayor Lurie: Trump call, federal deployment, and PG&E blackout communications

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Mayor Lurie: Trump call, federal deployment, and PG&E blackout communications
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The records are listed from most specific to most general. Please produce them on a rolling basis in the order listed, releasing the earlier items as soon as they are ready rather than holding them until the later, broader items are searched.

1. The date, time and duration of the phone call(s) between Mayor Daniel Lurie and President Trump on or about October 22, 2025, including call logs and calendar entries.
2. Records identifying everyone on that call (aides, staff, officials or private individuals) and their affiliations.
3. Any audio recordings or transcripts of that call.
4. Notes, memos or summaries of that call made by the Mayor's Office or any other City department.
5. All text messages between Mayor Lurie and PG&E's Jake Zigelman, December 19-31, 2025, as a complete thread with all timestamps, including the messages before and after the December 21, 2025 "opera house update" message.
6. The full group message thread started by Ned Segal on December 20, 2025 about the citywide blackout and the War Memorial Opera House (reportedly including Branislav Henselmann, Mary Ellen Carroll and Kate Sofis), from its start through December 31, 2025.
7. All text messages between Mayor Lurie and PG&E CEO Patti Poppe, December 19, 2025 through January 31, 2026.
8. All emails between Mayor Lurie and Jake Zigelman, December 19-31, 2025.
9. All text messages between Alicia John-Baptiste and Jake Zigelman, December 19-31, 2025.
10. All emails between Alicia John-Baptiste and Jake Zigelman, December 19-31, 2025.
11. Communications between the Mayor's Office and the Department of Homeland Security, ICE, CBP or any other federal agency about the planned federal deployment to San Francisco or its cancellation, October 8-31, 2025.
12. Communications with technology executives or other private individuals about the deployment, the call with President Trump, or efforts to influence the President's decision, October 8-31, 2025.
13. Communications from federal officials confirming or changing the deployment plans, October 8-31, 2025.
14. Records underlying the Mayor's public statement that the President told him the deployment was called off, and any follow-up documentation or internal evaluation of the cancellation.
15. Records of any verbal or written understanding between the Mayor's Office (or the City) and the federal government about the cancellation, and any City policy changes or commitments made as part of, or following, the call.
16. Records the City received giving notice of the planned deployment (dates, expected personnel, scope).
17. Records of the Mayor's October 22, 2025 executive directive and any other City preparations for the deployment.
18. Internal City memos assessing the deployment's impact on City operations, public safety or immigrant communities.
19. Coordination records among City departments (for example DEM, SFPD and the City Attorney) about preparing for or responding to federal action, October 8-31, 2025.
20. Emails, text messages, chat messages and memos that mention the call with President Trump or the planned federal deployment or its cancellation, October 8-31, 2025, including messages within the Mayor's Office, with other City officials, and with federal officials.
21. All emails sent or received by anyone in the Mayor's Office about the December 2025 blackouts or power restoration, December 19-31, 2025.
22. Any other written communications (emails, texts, chats, memos) between the Mayor or Mayor's Office staff and PG&E about the outages, December 20, 2025 through the date this request is fulfilled.

This request includes records on personal phones or accounts used for City business. Please provide text messages as complete threads with timestamps and sender/recipient, not cropped screenshots. If any record or part of a record is withheld, please identify it. Please also tell me which numbered items have no responsive records.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson

title: FDA's review of increased MedWatch reports involving extended-release ADHD stimulant medications

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FDA's review of increased MedWatch reports involving extended-release ADHD stimulant medications
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

concerning the FDA's review of increased MedWatch reports involving extended-release ADHD stimulant medications, as described in the agency's FY2024 Report on the State of Pharmaceutical Quality.

Specifically, the report stated:

“FDA is reviewing the recent increase in MedWatch reports for extended-release ADHD stimulant products to determine necessary responses, which may include additional information requests, sampling and testing, or inspections.”

I request the final assessment, decision memorandum, or most recent substantive status report documenting the findings, status, or disposition of this specific review.

I am particularly interested in whether FDA determined that further investigation was warranted, whether the review remains ongoing or has been closed, and whether any product-specific quality concerns were identified.

Date range: January 1, 2024, through the date this request is processed.

To keep this request narrowly focused, I am not seeking individual MedWatch reports, raw adverse-event data, manufacturer submissions, laboratory testing records, inspection reports, or general correspondence.

Please limit the search to the Office of Quality Surveillance within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research's Office of Pharmaceutical Quality, and any office directly responsible for documenting the conclusions or status of this specific review.

If no final assessment exists, please provide the most recent completed substantive status report, briefing memorandum, or decision document concerning the review. I am requesting existing records only and do not ask FDA to create a new report.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma Yasinski

title: data used to create Figure 9 of the FDA's FY2024 Report on the State of Pharmaceutical Quality

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: data used to create Figure 9 of the FDA's FY2024 Report on the State of Pharmaceutical Quality
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

the underlying numerical data used to create Figure 9 of the FDA's FY2024 Report on the State of Pharmaceutical Quality, which presents information concerning MedWatch reports, drug distribution volume, recalls, and approvals for stimulant ADHD medications.

Specifically, I request:

The existing spreadsheet, data table, or other electronic dataset containing the numerical values used to generate Figure 9.

Any existing accompanying data dictionary, methodology notes, or documentation necessary to interpret those values, including definitions of the measures and product categories represented.

Please preserve the original reporting years, product categories, numerical values, and column headings, including separate measures for MedWatch reports, distribution volume, recalls, and approvals, to the extent these are present in the underlying records.

I am requesting the existing data used to produce the published figure, not the underlying individual MedWatch case reports, patient-level records, manufacturer submissions, or source databases from which the figures may have been calculated.

To minimize processing time, please limit the search to the Office of Quality Surveillance within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research's Office of Pharmaceutical Quality, or the office responsible for preparing Figure 9.

I would prefer to receive the data in its original electronic format, such as Excel or CSV, rather than as a PDF or image. If the figure was generated using another format, I would welcome the original data file in that format.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Public Records Request – Columbiana Foundry Company, Columbiana, Ohio
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request concerns the facility's operations and physical plant, particularly during the period January 1, 1978, through December 31, 1984. Please include records created before or after that period to the extent they document historical site conditions, equipment, building materials, renovations, demolition, or asbestos-containing materials.

Please search electronic and available historical paper records, including records maintained by the relevant EPA district and air-pollution-control programs, for the following:

Asbestos surveys, asbestos-containing material inventories, bulk sampling results, laboratory analyses, asbestos abatement plans, and abatement completion reports.
Asbestos-related demolition or renovation notifications, including notifications submitted under the National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP), inspection reports, compliance records, and related correspondence.
Air permits, permit applications, facility descriptions, inspection reports, and records concerning the installation, replacement, modification, or removal of furnaces, cupolas, induction furnaces, heat-treatment furnaces, boilers, exhaust systems, and associated industrial equipment.
Facility site plans, building floor plans, equipment layouts, engineering drawings, construction or renovation documents, and records identifying the location or removal of thermal insulation or other potentially asbestos-containing building materials.
Environmental assessments, hazardous-material surveys, site investigations, sampling reports, remediation records, and communications concerning asbestos or other hazardous building materials at the facility.
Any historical records associated with the company's 1972 cupola-to-induction-furnace replacement project, including permit applications, project descriptions, equipment specifications, and related agency correspondence.

Please search under the names “The Columbiana Foundry Company,” “Columbiana Foundry Company,” and “Columbiana Foundry,” as well as the physical address and any historical facility identifiers located during your search.

If any responsive records are held by another agency or district office, please identify the appropriate custodian or forward this request if permitted. communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records relating to or mentioning Henry Wadsworth Longfellow Dana (January 26, 1881-April 26, 1950), aka Harry Dana or H. W. L. Dana. Dana was a scholar and educator at Columbia University and the New School for Social Research, among other places. He was a conscientious objector during World War I. He made multiple visits to Soviet Russia during the 1920s and 1930s. He lived most of his life in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and New York, New York.

I believe you have already released documents related to Dana, as some are cited in: Eliza Starr Byard, “Inverts, Perverts, and National Peril: Federal Responses to Homosexuality, 1890–1956 - ProQuest” (Dissertation, Columbia University, 2002).

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the ELSUR Records System, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records (as the Bureau has posted copies of records that it previously said were transferred to NARA such as the Tokyo Rose file).

I am a member of the academic community and request classification as such. I am a PhD Candidate in History at the CUNY Graduate Center, New York, NY. As such, my primary purpose is to use this information to write a dissertation to add to public knowledge and I therefore request that fees be waived. Per DOJ FOIA guidance, "a requester should be granted a fee waiver if the requested information (1) sheds light on the activities and operations of the government; (2) is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of those operations and activities; and (3) is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester." As this FOIA meets all of these requirements, a fee waiver is warranted.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Danielle Bennett

For items 1 and 2, please provide all maintained and exportable fields, including, where present, search timestamps, user names and identifiers, organization names and identifiers, search reasons, complaint or case numbers, search types, filters, date ranges searched, and counts of networks or devices searched. The reasons for a search, associated complaint number, and identity of the authorized inquirer are specifically addressed by General Order O-44.13, "Records."

3. Existing electronic records of the Department's inbound and outbound Flock network-sharing configuration as of the date the search for these records is conducted. Include the names and identifiers of organizations sharing their networks with the Department and organizations with which the Department shares its networks, together with the direction and status of each sharing relationship. Please provide existing settings exports or reports, or the underlying electronically retrievable configuration records in an available format.

4. Flock Safety Event Log.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Safety Event Log, including all maintained and exportable fields. Per Flock's documentation, the Event Log is available within the Insights tab. Flock customer support may be able to assist with the mass-downloading of this data if assistance is required.

The Organization Audit, Network Audit, and Event Log are identified by their Flock report names and their availability through the Insights tab. If these reports have been renamed or moved, please provide the equivalent records. Items 1, 2, and 4 seek audit and event records, rather than a bulk export of the underlying vehicle-sighting database or camera images.

Records relating to the Department's ALPR policy:

5.  All versions of written policies governing the deployment of automated license plate recognition cameras/readers/systems and the use, storage, retention, and sharing of data obtained through those systems that were created, revised, or in effect at any time from January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed. If particular entries or fields in an audit or event log are properly exempt, please redact those portions rather than withhold the entire report.

Please address each numbered item separately. For records the Department does not possess or cannot locate after a diligent search, please provide the certification contemplated by Public Officers Law Section 89(3)(a), identifying the relevant request item.
